finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.spec.ts::the central behavior change — list ordering and `updatedat` now sourced from postgres instead of the yorkie admin call — has no test at all
evidence: Verified against the supplied files: `document.controller.spec.ts` contains only the `createDocument` fileId-gating describe block, and its stub at line 13 is `{ getSummaries: jest.fn() } as never` — the controller now calls `getEditors` (document.controller.ts:65), so `attachMeta` is provably never exercised by that spec (it would throw on an undefined method). The new spec files added in this PR cover `updateDocument` (document.service.spec.ts), the webhook controller, the guard, and `parseYorkieDocKey`, but none assert the `updatedAt: d.updatedAt.toISOString()` sourcing or the `orderBy: [{updatedAt:'desc'},{createdAt:'desc'}]` on lines 116/148. The e2e list test in authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts stubs YorkieAdminService and only asserts list length and id, so ordering/updatedAt regressions would go undetected. Real gap, but the untested change is a straightforward field read plus orderBy, so impact is limited to future regression risk.
